title: Paper III  -  Cross-Domain Application

canonical_node.axiom: A principle that works in one domain is local; if it works in three independent domains, it is structural.
definitions: Structural isomorphism: shared logical architecture that constrains predictions in both domains.
Analogical similarity: pattern looks similar but does not constrain predictions.
Three-Domain Rule: a universal principle must work in at least three independent domains.
derivation: Paper I establishes a claim in an original domain.
Paper III applies the same claim to an unexpected domain.
If the claim produces novel testable predictions in the new domain, it is structural.
If it works in three independent domains, it is universal.
canonical_node.action: Apply the Paper I claim to an unexpected domain, test predictions, and assess structural isomorphism.
boundary: Does not claim universality from a single application.
Does not force analogies; must be structural.
test: Can the claim produce novel testable predictions in the new domain
Does the isomorphism constrain predictions in both domains
Does the application explain phenomena that existing domain theories do not

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Cross-domain validation of a principle, enabling universality assessment.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: The original claim remains intact; application does not alter it.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without cross-domain application, universality cannot be established.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Use as a template for cross-domain application; requires concrete instantiation.

risk.lean_target: A formal framework for detecting structural isomorphism across domains.

plain_summary: This document is a template for applying a claim from Paper I to an unexpected domain, with emphasis on structural isomorphism and kill conditions. It does not itself establish any empirical result.
